I have two garden ponds that I have recently cleaned out (about a years worth of leaves, sticks, and other debris as well as the filthy water have been removed and fresh clean water has been added). I wanted seek advice for plant life I should look to add as well as how I might go about keeping this water clean and clear. Thanks!

First, how big are they? Second, choose plants that grow slightly out side of the water (either floating or emergent). Floating plants like duckweed, water hyacinth, and water lettuce are fucking awesome. They gather a lot of excess nutrients and shade the water preventing massive algae blooms. Emergent plants like lotus, water lilly, and arrow leaf use what is called the "aerial advantage". This means that they breath CO2 from the air and not just the water, like most water plants. This is beneficial because water dissolves CO2 very poorly, constricting the growth of most water plants (even if well aerated with a pump or filter).

Also, will you be adding fish? Make sure to account for their bioload (shit, basically) as if nitrogen levels get too high algae blooms and worst case scenario - fish die. Don't, for example, try to stock koi in a 100 gallon pond. If you don't want fish, I would still recommend a few feeder minnows from the pet store to keep mosquito and insect populations down.
